initiative.name: Standardize internal approval requests before tooling
initiative.summary: Four departments submit approval requests through email and team chat, while a coordinator manually records status in a shared tracker. Definitions, routes, exceptions, and ownership differ, causing lost status and rework. The request is to define a minimum approval model and test existing capability before selecting or building a portal.
initiative.fit_rationale: The cross-functional coordination problem is material enough for structured discovery, but the mandatory controls, business owner, minimum process, and existing-system fit are unresolved.
scope_in: Define the minimum request and approval model
Clarify mandatory approvals and legitimate exceptions
Assess the owned work-management suite against the minimum model
Recommend a process and technology direction

target_state.desired_outcome: A traceable, consistently defined request-to-decision process that uses the simplest sustainable capability.

functional_requirements.statement: Capture the minimum information required for each approved request category.
functional_requirements.evidence: Inconsistent templates are an observed problem.

functional_requirements.statement: Route normal requests and legitimate exceptions to accountable approvers.
functional_requirements.evidence: Routes currently vary and depend on individual judgment.

functional_requirements.statement: Show current status and final decision to authorized participants.
functional_requirements.evidence: Status visibility is an observed problem.

nonfunctional_constraints.statement: Access and audit requirements must be confirmed before implementation.

human_controls: A policy owner approves the minimum process and exception rules
rollout_and_adoption: Test the minimum model with sanitized recent cases before configuring or building tooling
support_and_fallback: Retain the current channels during any bounded trial until ownership and recovery are defined

success_measures.name: Requests requiring rework because required information is missing

facts.statement: Four departments submit an estimated 20 to 40 requests per month.
Requests arrive through email and team chat and use different templates and routes.
The organization owns a work-management suite that may have relevant capability, but it has not been assessed.

interpretations.statement: Building a portal now would encode disputed or undocumented routing and exception rules.

dependencies_and_risks.statement: No accountable owner is confirmed for the end-to-end approval process.
dependencies_and_risks.consequence: Rules and exceptions cannot be standardized or maintained.
dependencies_and_risks.next_check: Identify the person who can approve the minimum process.

dependencies_and_risks.statement: Policy pages and person-held judgment may conflict or be stale.
dependencies_and_risks.consequence: A tool could automate incorrect routing or controls.
dependencies_and_risks.next_check: Review current policies and recent exceptions with accountable owners.

dependencies_and_risks.statement: Existing work-management capability has not been tested.
dependencies_and_risks.consequence: The team may procure or build functionality it already owns.
dependencies_and_risks.next_check: Run a sanitized configuration test after the minimum model is agreed.

limitations: Vendor research is premature until the minimum process and existing capability are assessed.

recommendation.rationale: Define the minimum approval model and its owner, then test the owned work-management suite before buying or building a portal.
caveats: Some approvals may still be removable.
The current volume is an estimate.
blocking_conditions: Do not approve custom development before rules, ownership, differentiation, lifecycle responsibilities, and total-cost inputs are established.
recommendation.next_decision: Assign the process owner and approve a short discovery to define the minimum model and test existing capability.

handoff.ticket_title: Standardize internal approval requests before tooling
handoff.ticket_body_markdown: Investigate and standardize the cross-functional approval-request process before selecting software. Requests currently arrive through email and team chat, a coordinator manually records status in a shared tracker, routes and exceptions vary, policy knowledge is only partly codified, and no end-to-end owner is named. Discovery should confirm mandatory controls, define the minimum request and approval model, identify accountable ownership, and test the owned work-management suite. Do not approve a custom portal until differentiation and full lifecycle ownership are evidenced.
